Strait of Hormuz Status: September 30, 2026 | Straits Daily Brief

Strait of Hormuz · Daily brief · UTC
30 September 2026 .
Brent $ 103.28 -0.21 % · Transits 1 (2026-09-27) · AI-assisted
01 UKMTO reports three tankers attacked in the Strait of Hormuz, per Yahoo, qcintel.com, and wanaen.com, with no major wire in this feed.

02 A crude oil tanker was struck on its port side by an unknown projectile in the strait on September 30, per The Maritime Executive and Lloyd's List.

03 Brent stood at $103.28, down 0.21% over 24 hours, as of 11:47 UTC; IMF PortWatch recorded 1 transit on 2026-09-27, against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day.

Situation
The Strait of Hormuz is seeing renewed direct strikes on commercial shipping, with UKMTO reporting three tankers attacked, per Yahoo, qcintel.com, and wanaen.com; no major wire in this feed carries it. Separately, The Maritime Executive and Lloyd's List report that a crude oil tanker was struck on its port side by an unknown projectile in the strait on September 30; the attacker has not been identified. A vessel also caught fire after a projectile strike, per Anadolu Ajansı, a development first reported in the earlier run of this brief and still without attribution of responsibility. The September 23 Cape Dao strike, in which an Indian seafarer was killed, continues to draw attention: The National reports the sailor's family is speaking publicly. Against this operational backdrop, Brent stood at $103.28, down 0.21% over 24 hours, as of 11:47 UTC. IMF PortWatch recorded 1 transit on 2026-09-27, against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day; a multi-day lag is expected given the weekly publication schedule. On the policy side, Iran's Foreign Minister set out a seven-day framework on September 25 that President Trump rejected publicly on September 26, and no new US response had been reported by the evening of September 29. Iran's Roads and Urban Development Minister described maritime transport as a sign of economic and diplomatic strength, per IRNA, which treats as a Tehran claim. As of 11:50 UTC, 134 AIS-visible vessels were holding position away from berth in the Strait of Hormuz and Gulf watch box, a count that leaves out ships within 25km of a working port. On the Hormuz Index, Crisis Pressure, the state composite, sits in the extreme band, with its value set by physical transit deviation alone; the Escalation Forecast sits in the elevated band, flagged low-confidence on thin contract volume, with the Brent-WTI forward spread as its top contributor.
